correctness.rationale: In the deterministic linear one-absorption-compartment periodic model with positive first-order rates a,b, positive weights w1,w2 and period T, periodic impulse profile G has integral over a period 1 and mean (w1+w2)/T. Expanding squared deviation yields phase variation 2w1w2[H(δ)-H(T/2)] where periodic autocorrelation sums the explicit difference of exponential tails. Re-derived R(s)=a²b²/[2(a+b)(b-a)]*(e^-a|s|/a - e^-b|s|/b) and periodic geometric-series identity. Penalty equals w1w2a²b²/[(a+b)(b-a)]*(F_a(d)-F_b(d)), F_r=(cosh(rd)-1)/(r sinh(rT/2)); integral F_r(d)=∫_0^d sinh(ry)/sinh(rT/2)dy decreases strictly in r for 0<y<T/2 because x*coth x increases. Hence unique anti-phase minimum for all distinct or coincident positive rates, including unequal doses; local quadratic coefficient positive. Independent numerical exact-formula penalty checks for a=1,b=4,T=1,w=(1,2) at d=.25,.5 gave 0.0487428383554 and 0.1163095966182; actual checker.py source separately integrates concentration with Simpson quadrature for rate/phase grids, including a=b. Quadrature diagnostic not infinite proof.
